html:
The Jelling stones are two runestones at Jelling in Jutland. The larger was raised about 965 by King Harald Bluetooth, who says on it that he won all Denmark and Norway and made the Danes Christian.

The smaller stone was set up by his father Gorm the Old for his wife Thyra. Between two great burial mounds Harald built a church, and moved his father's body into it. The big stone carries the oldest image of Christ in Scandinavia.

Danes call it the birth certificate of Denmark: the two stones carry the oldest mention of the name inside the country. Harald's conversion tied the kingdom to the German church and to the wider world of Christianity. His grandson Cnut would rule an empire across the North Sea.
